Given the structural conditions the chapter has assembled, art is not an optional cultural embellishment. It is what the conditions require once they obtain.

A person registers their own orientations (§8.1, §8.6). That registration has a feel — the internal aspect consciousness consists in. Some of the feel is propositionally expressible: someone can state what they have registered, and language will carry the statement across the interval to others (§8.10). But much of the feel is not propositional. The specific quality of grief at a particular loss, the specific texture of joy in a particular encounter, the specific weight of a particular memory — these are not paraphrasable. A paraphrase loses precisely what was to be transmitted. The content is the feel itself, not a description of the feel.

The prediction is conditional and sharp. Wherever sufficiently recursive social beings with non-propositional content needing transmission persist together in a medium with T, S, and Φ — and have materials and time enough to instantiate forms — the conditions for art are met, and the framework predicts that some form of made-object vehicle will arise to carry the content. The argument is conditional on those antecedents (recursion-depth sufficient for non-propositional registration; sociality sufficient for the transmission demand; materials and time enough to instantiate forms), and is a structural-tendency claim under those conditions, not a bare entailment from T/S/Φ alone. Once the conditions obtain, propositional transmission cannot carry the content without destroying it. Something else must do the carrying. That something is art.

Art therefore requires all the conditions the chapter has assembled. It requires Time because the form persists across a before and after, and because the feel unfolds rather than appears instantaneously. It requires Space because artist and audience occupy different positions, and the artifact crosses the interval between them without collapsing it. It requires Substance because the form must be made of something that holds its shape long enough to be encountered. It requires self-modeling in the artist, because only a being with an internal aspect has a feel to externalize. It requires self-modeling in the audience, because only a being with an internal aspect can have a feel reconstituted inside it. Remove any of these and art becomes structurally unavailable. Keep all of them, in beings sufficiently recursive and sufficiently social, and art becomes structurally predictable — what such beings do with non-propositional content given materials and time, given that no other channel will carry the content.

*Making and Resonance.* Art has two components the chapter's grammar keeps separate. Both are needed; neither alone is art.

The first is making. A person whose inside registers a particular orientation — a grief, a joy, a wonder, a terror, a tenderness, a recognition — shapes Substance into a form that answers to it. The artist does not transcribe the feel; transcription is language's operation, and language cannot carry this content. The artist instead builds a thing whose structure, when encountered, produces the feel in someone capable of receiving it. The craft of art is the craft of building such things. A song is a structure of sound in Time; a symphony or instrumental composition, the same operation at larger architecture. A painting is a structure of color and shape in Space; a drawing, of line and tone; a sculpture, of mass and surface in three dimensions; a photograph, of light caught at an instant; a work of architecture, of inhabited Space organized for the people who pass through it. A poem is a structure of language used for its sound, image, and rhythm rather than its propositional content; a novel or short story unfolds language across narrative Time; a piece of theater gathers bodies, voices, and language into one place for the duration of a performance. A dance is a structure of body moving through Space in Time. Craft — pottery, weaving, woodworking, glass, garment, tattoo, the well-shaped tool — works Substance into forms someone lives with daily, and remains art wherever the form is built so a feel can land in whoever takes it up. Comedy times sound, image, and silence so a recognition arrives as release. A film is a structure of many of these at once; an interactive medium like the video game folds the audience's own choices into the form. The materials differ; the operation does not. In each case the artist — composer, painter, sculptor, photographer, architect, poet, novelist, playwright, dancer, choreographer, actor, craftsperson, comedian, filmmaker, designer — has taken something internal, a feel that was theirs alone, and built an external form that will, if the craft succeeds, no longer be theirs alone. The same operation runs at scales the canon does not always honor. A curated social presence, a styled feed, a hosted dinner, a chosen wardrobe, a room arranged for a guest, the cadence of someone's everyday self-presentation — each *can be* the operation art consists in, but only when two conditions are jointly met. First, the making must be shaped for *resonance* — for a non-propositional feel landing in whoever encounters the form — rather than only for utility, status, persuasion, identification, or compliance with convention. Second, the form must hold together as a current in its own right, not merely as the sum of its functional parts; what it presents has to be a structured whole whose unity is what carries the feel. A wardrobe chosen for warmth and price is styled, but it is not yet art; a wardrobe chosen so a particular feel of selfhood can land in the people who encounter the wearer, and composed as a current whose unity carries that feel, is the operation, even if the result is not what gallery-and-museum aesthetics has historically named. The criterion separating art from styled-but-non-art presentation is not whether the maker has been licensed by an institution or the form ratified by a tradition; it is whether the form is built so a non-propositional content can land. By that criterion most curated social presence is *not* art — most is styling for status, identification, persuasion, or compliance with platform convention. Some of it is. The operation, not the medium, is what determines which.

The second is resonance. Someone else, elsewhere in Space or later in Time, encounters the form. If the form is well-made and the receiver is structured to take it up, the feel reconstitutes inside them. The audience does not learn what the experience was like; the audience has an experience structurally answerable to what the artist's was. Resonance is the name for that reconstitution. It is not metaphor. It is the structural operation that art exists to perform. The artist reached inward, produced a form, and the form reached outward to land in others who recognized the feel as one they themselves could have had. Without resonance, making is mere manufacture: an object produced, no feel transmitted. Without making, resonance has nothing to happen through. Art is the full arc.

The arc explains why art is not identical to self-expression. A person can express their inside without producing anything another could resonate with — a private scream, a journal read by no one, a dance performed alone. Expression is sufficient if the person only needs to externalize. Art requires the further essential feature: the form must be shaped so the feel can land elsewhere. That is why craft matters. That is why not all expression is art and not all art is expression. Art is expression engineered for resonance.
